header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, KARACHI
Date Order with signature of Judge
M/s. Ghulam Rasool Mangi and Muhammad Naseem, advocates for the applicants alongwith the applicants.
Mr. Iqbal Kalhoro, Addl. Prosecutor General, Sindh for the State.
body: By this common order, I propose to dispose of the above titled six criminal bail applications, as they relate to the same incident, which had taken place on 06.10.2008 between 0315 hours to 0520 hours within the jurisdiction of Police Station Mehmoodabad, Jamshed Town, South Zone, Karachi and has resulted in lodging of F.I.Rs. No. 317, 319, 320, 321 and 322 of 2008. For convenience sake, contents of one of the F.I.R. No.217/2008 are reproduced as under:

“That in between 5/6 of 10/2008, I, Sub Inspector Riaz Hussain and A.S.I. Hikmatullah, A.S.I. Haroon, HC Mumtaz Ghondal 14377, HC Shahdab Akhtar, PC Barkaat 17151, PC Tahir 8934, PC Abdul Khalique 17550, PC Aslam 15500 was on patrolling duty for prevention of crimes, during the patrolling myself sub inspector received spy information that one narcotic seller Farooq alias Farooqa and his accompanies are trying to shift the narcotics and weapons from the ada situated at Masoom Shah Colony, Kaala Pull to some other place, on this information, I informed the police station to duty office Inspector Muzaffar Ahmed on phone and called to Government mobiles for which Sub Inspector Muzaffar Ahmed along with two mobiles reached to me. I sub inspector alongwith police party went towards the Kaala Pull through railway line at about 1315 hours towards Farooq Adda, when they saw us near to them for which Farooq and his accompanies acted illegally, while interfering in the official duty in order to save themselves from their arrest started firing upon us form their weapons for which the police party in reply started indiscriminate firing upon them in self defence for their arrest, out of them one accused Waseem alias Singhania s/o Abdul Latif holding pistil 30 bore loaded bullet was arrested and the remaining accused managed to escape their good, while taking the benefit of darkness and narrow street and in the area one School bag black colour was found which was lying near about, one rifle SMG load four magazines 103 number and one rifle 222 three magazine load 85 bullets, I opened the bag and found 9MM bullets 145 numbers and in plastic thalie found the white heroin power and so also in the second white thalie the heroin powder was found, out of the recovered stuff, which was weighing found one kilo 500 grams and from the second thalie brown heron powder weighing 750 grams found, out of the while colour powder 10 grams and from brown heroin powder 10 grams were separated at the spot for the chemical examination and the remaining white power 1 kilo 490 grams and brown powder 740S grams were sealed separately, arrested accused Waseem alias Singhania s/o Abdul Latif disclosed that School bag black colour 9MM SMG load four magazines 103 bullets belongs to Farooq alias Farooqa, who went away while throwing, and 222 rifle load magazine 3 bullets 85 belongs to Irfan s/o Farooq, so also brown colour heroin powder belongs to Irfan, who fled away while throwing, whereas one remaining companions Haroon Khan and Naveed also escaped while firing. In the absence of private witnesses, officers were acted as a mashirs, arrested accused Waseem alias Singhania recovered pistol from him load magazine 4 bullets and SMG rifle bullets 103, four magazine 222 rifle, three magazines 85 bullets were sealed separately from the place of incident, empty shells of SMG four in numbers 30 bore pistol and 222 rifle 5 empty bullets were taken into police custody and sealed separately, mashirnama was prepared on spot. Accordingly, against arrested accused offence under Section 13-D of the Arms Ordinance were registered. Further accused Waseem alias Singhania s/o Abdul Latif, and the run away accused Farooq alias Farooqa, Irfan s/o Farooq were booked under Section 13-E of Arms Ordinance separately, out of the recovered heroin powder in whiter colour, brown colour separate F.I.R. under Section 6/9-C of Narcotic Act is being registered.”

2. First F.I.R. No.317/2008 under Section 352, 324, 34, PPC relates to the incident of ineffective firing and recovery of unlicensed weapons. The Second and Fourth F.I.Rs. No.319 and 321 of 2008 relate to the commission of offence under Section 13-E of the Arms Ordinance, while the Third and Fifth F.I.Rs. No.320 and 322 of 2008 relate to the commission of offence punishable under Section 6/9(c) of the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997. As evident from the contents of the above reproduced F.I.R., it is an incident of ineffective firing with no recovery of any arms or ammunition or narcotic substances from the person of the applicants. The recovery is shown from the place of incident with the further allegations that the applicants succeeded to make their escape good from the place of occurrence.

3. Mr. Iqbal Kalhoro, learned Addl. Prosecutor General, Sindh for the State looking to the above noted salient features of the case, candidly conceded that the case of the applicants need further enquiry as to their guilt and involvement in the commission of crime and also the possibility of their false and mala-fide involvement in these crimes cannot be ruled out.

4. After careful examination of the material placed on record, particularly, the contents of the five F.I.Rs., I am of the opinion that the case of all the applicants need further enquiry as to their quilt and involvement in the commission of crimes. More so, as the possibility of their mala-fide involvement also cannot be ruled out.
5. This being the position, interim pre-arrest bail allowed to the applicants vide orders dated 19.11.2008 and 04.12.2008 is confirmed in the same terms.
